proposal.utterance: What kind of BFO entity is the disposition to recognize authority?

entities.label: DispositionToRecognizeAuthority
entities.rationale: The disposition to recognize authority is an internally grounded, specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent (person, institution, or collective) and reflects a stable tendency or capacity to acknowledge and defer to authority structures. BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) is appropriate because: (1) it is specifically dependent — it inheres in a particular bearer; (2) it is internally grounded in the nature of that bearer (e.g., socialization, normative commitment, cognitive schema), distinguishing it from a Role which is externally grounded; (3) it is realizable — it can be manifested in acts of recognition (BFO_0000015 processes such as ActOfAcknowledgment already in the ontology). It differs from ActorWill (already typed as BFO_0000016) in that it is specifically directed at authority rather than volitional agency in general.

relations.rationale: DispositionToRecognizeAuthority is a subclass of BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016), inheriting its internally grounded, specifically dependent, realizable character.

When realized, the disposition to recognize authority is manifested in processes of the ActOfAcknowledgment class (BFO_0000015), already present in the ontology. BFO_0000054 (realized in) connects a realizable entity to the process that realizes it.

open_questions: Should DispositionToRecognizeAuthority be restricted to human agents, or also apply to collective/institutional bearers such as LegalInstitution?
Is the intent to model this as a general class (a kind of disposition) or as a specific individual instance (e.g., the disposition of a particular official or population)?
Should this disposition be related to CourtAuthority or LegalLegitimacyCondition already in the ontology, and if so, how (e.g., as a precondition or realizer)?

Is this disposition best understood as grounded in social practice (closer to a collective disposition) or in individual psychology — this may affect whether it inheres in a person (BFO_0000040) or a collective/institutional material entity?
proposal.rationale_summary: The disposition to recognize authority maps cleanly onto BFO_0000016 (Disposition) because dispositions are specifically dependent continuants that are internally grounded in their bearer and realizable in processes. Unlike a Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally conferred by social context, a disposition is rooted in the intrinsic nature or normative orientation of the bearer. The bearer here would be an agent — individual or collective — whose trained or socialized nature inclines it to acknowledge authority. When exercised, this disposition is realized in acknowledgment processes (ActOfAcknowledgment, already in the ontology). I propose minting DispositionToRecognizeAuthority as a new class under BFO_0000016, linked via rdfs:subClassOf, and asserting that instances of this class are realized in ActOfAcknowledgment processes via BFO_0000054. The class is distinguished from the existing ActorWill (also BFO_0000016) by its specific directedness toward authority structures rather than general volitional agency.
